model:
Riot Platforms business-model profile (built 30 October 2026 from the FY25 10-K, the 2Q26 10-Q, release and deck, and 2026 8-Ks; refresh when the FY26 10-K is filed).

1. Economic engine. Riot owns about 1.7 GW of approved Texas grid power (Rockdale 700 MW interconnection, owned in fee simple since January 2026; Corsicana 1 GW with about 400 MW built) plus about 192 MW in Kentucky, and is converting it from bitcoin mining into build-to-suit data center leases, using mining cash flow and bitcoin sales to fund the equity while project debt funds most of the build (10-K, 10-Q, 2Q26 deck).

2. Revenue map. Data center rent = leased critical IT MW x $/kW-month x 12, with annual escalators; tenant fit-out revenue is cost-plus and low margin (13% gross margin in 2Q26) and should be excluded from run-rate. Contracted: AMD 50 MW at Rockdale (initial 25 MW for about $311mn over 10 years, about $104/kW-month, modified gross lease with escalators; 50 MW averages about $63.6mn a year, about $106/kW-month); a leading frontier AI lab (named Anthropic PBC in the 10-Q's XBRL tags and by KBW) 191 MW for about $9.1bn over a 20-year initial term (about $457mn a year on average, about $199/kW-month; two five-year extensions take potential value to about $16.1bn). Total about $9.8bn on 241 MW. Rent starts as halls deliver: AMD 25 MW billing since May 2026, 10 MW due November 2026, 15 MW May 2027; AI lab 96 MW December 2027 and 95 MW June 2028. Bitcoin mining revenue = BTC mined (1,587 in 2Q26, 44.4 EH/s deployed) x BTC price, less power at about 3.6 c/kWh net of curtailment credits. Engineering (ESS Metron, E4A) sells switchgear and electrical services ($37.3mn 2Q26 revenue, $177.1mn backlog, 90% data center).

3. Cost structure. Mining: power ($73.5mn in 2Q26) under the Rockdale fixed-price PPA (345 MW: 195 MW through April 2030, 150 MW through October 2027), with ERCOT demand response and 4CP credits ($10.1mn in 2Q26, $30.6mn in 3Q25); cost to mine $49,912 per BTC ex depreciation, 69.6% of production value, 126.5% including miner depreciation. Data center: management targets an 80% to 90% NOI margin over the lease term; 2Q26 operating lease gross margin 84% (base rent 91%). Depreciation $97.8mn in 2Q26, mostly miners on 3-year lives (buildings 10 to 25 years, facility equipment 5 to 10). Stock-based compensation $35.6mn a quarter. Interest is small today (2Q26 expense $2.7mn; Coinbase interest capitalized) but rises as project debt is drawn.

4. Capital and funding. Build cost about $11mn to $12mn per critical IT MW for new construction (AI lab capex $2.1bn to $2.3bn including contingency) versus about $3.6mn per MW for the AMD retrofit of an existing building ($89.8mn for 25 MW; $170.2mn for 50 MW). Funding plan per the 2Q26 deck: AI lab debt at 80% to 90% loan-to-cost ($1.7bn to $2.1bn) after an investment-grade backstop is finalized, bridged by a $573mn Morgan Stanley senior secured delayed-draw loan (SOFR + 2.75%, non-recourse to the parent, maturing 31 December 2026 per the 14 August 8-K); equity of $210mn to $460mn, of which about $180mn is to come from a term loan on AMD's first 25 MW, leaving $30mn to $280mn from the balance sheet; AMD's second 25 MW ($81mn) funded by a $69mn delayed-draw loan at 85% LTC. Parent: 0.75% converts due 2030 ($594.4mn, conversion price about $14.86), revolvers ($54.3mn drawn), a $200mn Coinbase bitcoin-backed loan prepaid on 21 September 2026, a $500mn ATM unused at 30 June, and bitcoin (11,380 BTC at 30 June, $666.0mn; 9,665 BTC sold in H1 for $732.5mn).

5. Sensitivities. Bitcoin price and network hash rate (funding source until rent ramps); tenant credit and the backstop (sets the cost and advance rate of project debt); delivery timing (rent starts only on delivery); interest rates and credit spreads (takeout pricing, cap rates on unleased power); construction cost against the $11mn to $12mn per MW budget; ERCOT large-load rules; and the end of the 150 MW fixed-price PPA block in October 2027.

6. Competitive position. Power already approved and energized outside the ERCOT batch process (per the CEO), owned land at Rockdale, in-house switchgear and electrical engineering (ESS Metron, E4A) that shortens long-lead procurement, and a delivered-on-time first tenant (AMD). Competes with Cipher, TeraWulf, Core Scientific, IREN, Hut 8, Galaxy and Applied Digital for AI lab and hyperscaler leases; the 2Q26 deck claims one of the lowest EV per 2027 MW multiples in the group.

7. What would break the model. (a) The investment-grade backstop for the AI lab lease is not finalized, so takeout debt is smaller or dearer and the bridge must be extended or replaced with parent money. (b) Delivery slips at Rockdale push rent past the December 2027 and June 2028 dates while capex peaks in 2Q to 3Q27. (c) A falling bitcoin price and rising hash rate shrink the mining cash flow and the bitcoin treasury that fund the equity, forcing ATM issuance. (d) Corsicana does not convert from LOI to lease, leaving about 1 GW valued as unleased power when credit is tightening. (e) Cost overruns beyond the contingency on a $2.1bn to $2.3bn build.
